decisions.lexical_head: informité: negative informitas versus historical conformation
decisions.reason: CNRTL-TLFi derives informité from Latin informitas, absence of form; Godefroy’s Lexique de l’ancien français separately defines the same spelling as conformation next to information in the forming/instruction sense. The saved corpus aggregate lacks sentence-level sense evidence. These conflicting historical lexical branches were investigated, but neither branch can be assigned to the entire measured lemma record. Keep genuinely uncertain without claiming a sense-frequency split. Exact finite source-token review: no universal spelling replacement, substring rule, corrected lemma or fabricated corpus evidence. All measured source fields and independent routes are preserved.

review_scope: Finite native regional/historical forms, voseo preterites and transparent nominal compounds; one unrelated geological head and one investigated historical homonym. Dictionaries establish heads, while finite productive inference is explicitly identified. No broad classifier.
